messages:
Alex: FYI customer AcmeCorp is seeing truncated SSE responses. Final JSON object never arrives and finish_reason is absent. They hit it in prod after an intermittent proxy 302 redirect. Request id: r-0a1b2c3d.
Priya: can you paste the raw curl or SDK repro and any headers? 302 from a proxy is unusual for streaming.
Alex: repro below (sanitized):
```bash
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" \ \
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \ \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/stream?model=redwood-2
```
Observed output ends with: 
```
data: {"id":"tok_123","text":"...final partial"}

```
no trailing `data: [DONE]` or finish_reason. Server logs show intermittent: `proxy-ghi 302 Found -> upstream://stream-01` then `upstream closed connection` and client observes immediate EOF.
Mateo: 302 mid-stream could mean the proxy is doing a redirect for auth refresh or sticky session reshuffle. Do we have x-forwarded-proto / resume headers preserved?
Alex: headers we saw: `x-request-id: r-0a1b2c3d`, `x-auth-rotate: in-progress`, `x-billing-cust: acme-123`. Proxy returned a short 302 with `Location: https://auth.internal/rotate` and `Connection: close`.
Lina: Customer is hitting rate limits? They're on Dedicated burst. They reported 6 truncated streams in the last hour, impact: UI shows `…` and never completes. Need ETA and mitigation.
Priya: repro attempt plan: 1) run curl loop to reproduce intermittent 302, 2) try node-fetch streaming with keepalive and inspect resume headers, 3) capture tcpdump during event to confirm proxy sends FIN vs full SSE close. Mateo can you check proxy config for 302 during backend rolling updates?
Mateo: I'll check. Quick workaround: client-side handle EOF as potential final token and call the v1/resume endpoint with the last-emit id to request remaining tokens — we need to document resume semantics for auth-rotate cases.
streambot: alert: spike of `stream_eof_unexpected` for customer acme-123 (6 events in 1h) — created ticket #INC-2026.
Alex: repro steps we gave to Acme: send a long generation (2k tokens) with streaming, then trigger auth rotation (we simulated by returning 302 from an nginx proxy). Result: final JSON object truncated, no finish_reason, client parse error.
Priya: can you attach a small sanitized HAR or the SSE raw bytes? specifically want to see if the last bytes include a partial JSON trailing `,` or unclosed brace. Also need the server side instance logs for the r-0a1b2c3d request to confirm runtime emitted the finisher.
Alex: attached snippet showing server wrote final `data: {"finish_reason":null,"id":"tok_123"}

` then upstream socket reset. So runtime did send finisher but proxy closed before it reached client.
Mateo: then fix is on proxy path: ensure proxy buffers and forwards until full SSE event flushed, or make it transparent for 302 when Authorization header present. I'll open a patch to nginx conf to `proxy_ignore_client_abort off` and increase `proxy_buffering` for event-streams.
Lina: customer wants a short-term mitigation we can recommend: 1) use our non-streaming generation (synchronous) for critical paths, or 2) enable client resume (if integrated) to re-request remainder.
Priya: also adding server-side defensive change: emit an extra small keepalive SSE `data: {"fin":true}` before final chunk so proxies are more likely to flush. I'll open a PR for both docs + runtime fallback for finish_reason absent (treat EOF after valid JSON prefix as final).
Alex: I'll reply to Acme with repro, temporary mitigations, and INC-2026 ticket id. Thanks — keep me posted here.
Mateo: noted, pushing proxy config patch to canary in us-west-2.
Priya: logging todo: add correlation `x-stream-resume` header to resumable requests so we can match resume attempts.
Lina: thx team. Customer wants ETA ~ 24h.
Alex: assigning owner: Priya for runtime fix, Mateo for proxy patch, Lina for CS comms.
Priya: created GH issue: redwood/runtime#4821 (runtime fallback + extra keepalive).
Mateo: created infra change: infra/proxy#1293 (nginx buffering tweak).
Lina: ping when canary is done and we'll roll communication out. :thumbsup:
